summary: A 1936 Aermotor lookout in the Bradshaw Mountains above Prescott, staffed by a volunteer in fire season and reached by trail; sources disagree on height and elevation.

facts.design: Modified L-4 cab on a 30 ft Aermotor MC-24 tower (register)

access.note: A rough road reaches the summit, but most people hike the Groom Creek Trail. A Forest Service page says the Spruce Mountain picnic site sits behind a gate that is locked when the tower is not staffed.

visit.trail_note: Groom Creek Trail to a fire road (about two hours by the blog's account), then about a quarter mile to the summit. Visitors are encouraged to climb while the volunteer is on duty (blog, undated).

events.note: First used as a daily patrol lookout
Timbers cut for a new tower in June 1921; new lookout station under construction in July 1921
Small fire believed to be the year's first lightning fire, first reported from the lookout station in July 1921; lookout F.M. Mulkins on duty
Lookout Dwight Morris cut down a lightning-struck pine to smother the fire
Register gives construction in 1936; a blog says the CCC built it. Sources do not say whether this replaced the 1921 tower.
Ranger Turney placed a new lookout; A. Starker Leopold, a University of California forestry student, was the lookout
Forest Service reported the fire lookout had been put back on Spruce Mountain
Registered August 5, 2003 as US 531, AZ 53; nominated by Dave Lorenz

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register details list 7,633 ft (2,327 m); the register's own description gives 7693 ft. The story reports both figures and does not pick one.
Register and older records give a 30-ft tower; the blog says visitors climb 55 ft to reach the lookout. No source read explains the difference, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The azrock.org 2022 post was read but not used: it calls the tower wood and stone and no longer in use and gives a 7,255 ft peak, both at odds with the other sources. Current staffing rests on an undated blog and an undated Forest Service page, so a dated source would strengthen it. Flickr photos (alanenglish) turned up in search but were not read or added. The CCC attribution comes only from the blog.
